beats.trigger: ## Multi-Agent Systems
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The filesystem is the meeting room.
beats.got: Agents hand work to each other through files. The 'hire' metaphor is a bit cute.

beats.trigger: Schedule your personal agent to read your challenge memory for a week.
beats.got: Homework I did not do. Nothing new.

beats.trigger: **Create** a framework-guided answer to a strategic question about your challenge
beats.got: A list of verbs. It looks like every programme's learning objectives slide.

beats.trigger: Three agents search Confluence, OneDrive and practitioner articles, and three more decide what it means.
beats.got: Concrete enough. Our own Confluence is a mess, so I'm curious what it finds.

beats.trigger: Writing a file changes your folder. Slack changes another system.
beats.got: The agent drafts the message, a human approves it, and it stops when unsure. That is a sensible boundary and not hype.

beats.trigger: Push back when the first answer restates the problem.
beats.got: It first handed my own problem back to me. Pushing made it name a sharper decision. Useful, but I can do that in a meeting too.

beats.trigger: If an agent starts reading the world, stop it, steer narrower, then say *"continue"*.
beats.got: Three sessions pulled material from wiki, docs and web in parallel. That would have been a day of someone's work two years ago. Reasonably impressive.

beats.trigger: You can't yet tell if the answer is right. That is expected.
beats.got: The synthesis reads well, and they admit I cannot yet tell whether it is true. That candour is why I trust the rest a bit more.

beats.trigger: When do you split, and how?
beats.got: A question, fair enough.

beats.trigger: A hundred tiny agents cost more to coordinate than they save.
beats.got: One agent per recurring job. It is the same org-design lesson we know from teams.

beats.trigger: Default to one agent with a good prompt.
beats.got: The training tells me not to use its own headline trick by default. A vendor rarely says that.

beats.trigger: A backward planner and a reframer in the same voice are one agent pretending to be two.
beats.got: Three tests for splitting: access, dialect, stance. I can apply them to any case.

beats.trigger: More input does not fix a beige answer.
beats.got: More agents do not add rigour. It is a warning against theatre.

beats.trigger: The synthesizer then commits to one diagnosis and drops what does not serve it.
beats.got: Give it a framework and it stops averaging. Rumelt is fine, though the drop-what-doesn't-serve-it part sounds like it could also drop inconvenient facts.

beats.trigger: Could one prompt produce the same quality of output?
beats.got: A simple test, and it argues against overbuilding.

beats.trigger: Each helper gets one job, reports back as a file and disappears.
beats.got: Separate sessions for long-lived agents, helpers inside one session for quick jobs.

beats.trigger: **Pick:** Sessions for agents that stay alive; helper agents for in and out.
beats.got: Nothing new. It repeats the previous slide.

beats.trigger: A retriever finds two numbers and the curator keeps one.
beats.got: Failures show up at handoffs, as in any organisation. The example is concrete.

beats.trigger: If one well-prompted agent does the job, write that prompt.
beats.got: Nothing new. It is the third time they've said it.

beats.trigger: three views averaged into mush
beats.got: A list of failure modes, which is honest.

beats.trigger: Prompt your stuck system to diagnose whether the bug lives in the sources, the processing, or the boundary between agents.
beats.got: You ask the agent to debug itself and it names where the fault is. Practical.

beats.trigger: add a rule to CLAUDE.md: what to read first, what not to smooth over, which output format to produce, when to stop and ask.
beats.got: Fixes go into a rules file, so the lesson persists. It's a reasonable discipline.

beats.trigger: It does not check whether the briefing is true.
beats.got: The audit checks the handoffs but not the truth of the result. A plain statement of what does not work yet. This is the best slide so far.

beats.trigger: Push back where the summary is wrong
beats.got: Argue with the summary, as you would with a junior analyst.

beats.trigger: The synthesized briefing's correctness stays an open question today.
beats.got: I leave with a briefing I cannot verify. They say so. Honest, but a bit unsatisfying.

beats.trigger: Optional move: pressure-test the memory.
beats.got: Optional homework I will skip.

beats.trigger: Split only where agents can't be one: access, dialect, stance.
beats.got: A good summary. Split only for access, dialect or stance.

beats.trigger: Pre-reads before Module 4
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Agents add non-deterministic behaviour, prompt injection (direct, or inside retrieved text) and emergent capability you can only bound.
beats.got: Normal security still applies, and agents add new risks. This is the compliance conversation that will actually come up at my company.

beats.trigger: An agent that works across connected systems has access to those systems.
beats.got: The right question for my legal team: what is the worst it could do with that access?

beats.trigger: keep working on your real problem
beats.got: Keep going on a real problem. Fine.

take_homes: Start with one agent. Split only when the data or tool access differs, the source dialects differ, or you want real disagreement. More agents does not mean more rigour.
Problems appear at the handoffs between agents, and nothing here checks whether the final briefing is true.
Keep an agent that writes a draft and waits for approval before it touches another system such as Slack.

monday.move: Run the three-retriever setup once on a real telecom partnership question, and check the synthesis against what I already know.
monday.who: Me, alone first. Nobody else until I have seen whether it holds up.
monday.when: Next week, if the calendar allows.
monday.stop_condition: The briefing is wrong or beige on something I know well, or the setup needs more tuning than the question is worth.
monday.blocker: Steering group calendar, and whether I am allowed to point it at the company wiki.

misconception.why: I expected the same slides with AI written on them. The three-retriever exercise was something I couldn't have done two years ago, and the module said plainly that it can't verify the answer and tells you not to split by default. I still don't know whether it lasts.

one_line: Surprisingly honest: it spends half the time telling you not to use multiple agents, and the retriever exercise showed me something new.
